title: Two-day date errors permit both April warmth slope signs for beech leaf-date spread at eight Swiss stations in 1961-2020
abstract: We tested April warmth and the spatial spread of beech leaf dates at eight fixed Swiss stations in 1961-2020. Four tests covered two regions and two periods. Slopes ranged from -1.36 to -0.35 days per degree C. All four corrected confidence intervals included zero. Exact bounds allowed each date to differ from its report by up to two days. These bounds permit both slope signs in all four samples. We used linear programs and all interval-box vertices to find annual spread limits, then constructed date assignments that attain each slope limit. Larger networks complete within each period also gave uncertain slopes. Eight selected stations, coarse monthly weather and missing visit logs limit inference. This study does not identify a causal climate effect and tests no pollutant or daily extreme. The package includes source hashes, transformed evidence, code, results, checks and figures.

display.caption: Fixed-station spatial spread and April temperature slopes. All four corrected intervals include zero.
Exact fixed-record slope bounds for one-day and two-day date errors. These are possibility bounds, not confidence intervals.
